name: Breaker
tagline: An engine that finally goes idle: less GPU with nothing moving, less memory, and lyrics that only wake for the words.

highlights.title: The GPU rests when nothing moves
highlights.body: Wavee used to hold the graphics chip at half load with nothing on screen changing: every awake frame repainted the whole window, a scrollbar that was still fading when you left a page kept the loop running for the rest of the session, and a pending tooltip, a hovered scrollbar or an open lyrics panel each re-rendered every single frame. Frames now repaint only what changed, blurred and faded surfaces included, and the loop idles the moment the last thing settles. On a Snapdragon laptop an idle album page went from about 55 % GPU to 0 %.

highlights.title: Lighter in memory
highlights.body: The weak-GPU budgets that never applied now do, album art is budgeted at the size the GPU actually commits, a finished video releases its decoder instead of keeping it for the session, the memory governor can finally free something, and a soft-edged list no longer leases a 56 MB scratch surface to fade a few pixels. Matched runs on the same profile show a smaller working set and a lower peak, and the app tracks every graphics allocation at the size the driver reports.

highlights.title: Lyrics and playback, quieter
highlights.body: Open lyrics wake only for the words: an instrumental intro, a break between verses or an outro costs nothing, and the karaoke wipe still lands on the exact syllable. Paused lyrics stop repainting, artwork no longer flashes during playback, a pause can no longer be undone by a late position report, and hidden level meters and neutral effects skip their audio work entirely.
